title: A laboratory-data model classifies retrospective COVID-19 severity labels
summary: Tuned logistic regression in 8,844 repeated blood tests from 2,935 unvaccinated patients estimated retrospective COVID-19 severity labels, reporting an AUC of 0.8512. Tuning raised sensitivity from 36.59% to 78.05% while lowering specificity from 96.38% to 77.00%. This internal test-level evaluation does not establish early prognosis for new patients.
organization: University of Alicante; University and Polytechnic La Fe Hospital of Valencia

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: se0030, se0080, se0120, se0150, se0160. Primary-source caveat and denominator review; candidate-panel identity corrected where relevant.

evidence.ai_role: Logistic regression fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: Five-fold stratified evaluation split blood tests, approximately 7,075 for training and 1,769 for testing per fold; model and scaler combinations were compared and logistic regression was tuned.
evidence.unknown: Patient grouping across folds is not established. Availability-based feature selection and model tuning are not shown to be nested within independent patient-level validation; multiple tests per patient can inflate apparent generalization. Samples after ICU admission were excluded; no prospective benefit or new biomarker mechanism is established. Model/scaler selection used evaluation folds. A figure caption and cohort breakdown describe the nonsevere group differently; no conclusion about hospitalization status is drawn. The operating-point tradeoff is distinct from the small AUC change from 0.8418 to 0.8512.
